newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Chretien says majority important.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Chretien says majority important.

text.p: Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien said on Tuesday that a strong majority government was useful for his government to pursue its agenda.

"It's always good to have a strong majority," Chretien told reporters after addressing a crowd of about 1,000 Liberal supporters at a breakfast rally. "Look at what we managed to do in the last term. Having a majority, we had to do tough things that might not have been possible in a minority government."

A Reuters poll by Zogby International on Tuesday showed that Canada's ruling Liberals were losing support, even in their Ontario stronghold, and faced the prospect of a reduced majority in the June 2 election.

Pollster John Zogby said the poll showed a minority government "is within the realm of possibility. It's too close to call right now," he said. "Chretien will no doubt win, but his power in a second term can be greatly diminished."
Asked about recent polls showing the possibility of a reduced majority -- and maybe even a minority government if support eroded further, Chretien responded. "I never comment on polls."
In the 1993 election, the Liberals won 177 of the 295 parliamentary seats, with 41 percent of the vote.
The latest survey, conducted from May 24 to May 26, showed the Liberals with 40.7 percent of support, with their lead over the second-place Conservatives trimmed to 18.7 points.

The Reuters-Zogby poll mirrors another poll released on Tuesday suggesting a slimmer Liberal majority. The poll by Ekos Research Associates gave the Liberals 37.8 percent, with 21.2 percent for the Conservatives, 17.7 percent for Reform, 11.3 percent for the NDP and 9.7 percent for the Bloc.
